subject: Re: CloudForge — temporary SLO amendment & onboarding credits
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@cloudforge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cloudforge.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Temporary SLO amendment & pricing relief during onboarding

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the onboarding walkthrough last week — the team is excited to get Redwood into production. We ran a short pilot and saw repeated tail-latency spikes during our batch ingestion windows. Our SREs think the pattern is largely input-shape related and tied to our highest-concurrency flows during imports.

Given the risk to our initial go-live on Sept 15, CloudForge is asking for two temporary, non-standard items to reduce our launch risk:

- A temporary SLO floor of 99.5% uptime for the first 90 days (instead of the standard 99.95%),
- A reduced service-credit exposure (cap credits at 2% of monthly invoice or $10k, whichever is lower) plus a commercial credit of 20% off host fees for month 1–3 while we complete performance tuning.

We understand these are exceptions; we are prepared to sign a short-term amendment and accelerate our optimization work with Redwood’s SRE team (we offered to run additional telemetry). Could you route this to the deal desk and leadership for quick approval? We are targeting a Sept 15 go-live and need clarity on terms by next Thu (Sept 3).

Attaching our onboarding checklist and sample import traces.

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Platform
CloudForge

Attachments: onboarding_traces.zip (log archive), CF_onboarding_checklist.pdf (PDF)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: Temporary SLO amendment & pricing relief during onboarding

Team — forwarding CloudForge's ask. TL;DR: customer wants a 90-day, temporary SLO floor at 99.5% + credit cap and a short-term commercial credit (20% month 1–3). They need decision by Sept 3 to keep their Sept 15 go-live.

Why this matters: CloudForge is a high-fit account (large seat count, public cloud security posture) and a fast win for our marketplace pipeline. If they delay go-live we risk losing the pilot momentum and increased costs for both sides.

Requesting executive sign-off for a limited, documented exception that includes:
- Temporary SLO floor: 99.5% for 90 days starting at go-live;
- Limited service-credit exposure: cap credits to 2% of monthly invoice or $10k;
- Commercial concession: 20% hosting credit months 1–3 conditioned on close cooperation on perf work;
- Clause: automatic reversion to standard SLA and normal remedies after 90 days.

Attached are their traces and a one-page proposed term sheet I drafted (proposed-slo-redline.docx). I recommend approving conditionally and have legal/finance sign-off before DocuSign.

Please reply with approval / edits. If we need a faster path, happy to escalate to Rishi for an exec quick-check today.

Thanks,
Vivek
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Temporary SLO amendment & pricing relief during onboarding

Vivek — thanks for the summary and the term sheet draft. I reviewed the proposed language. A few points from deal desk/legal perspective:

1) We can accept a timeboxed SLO floor (99.5%) provided we get:
   - A clear start date tied to production traffic and a mutual acceptance checklist;
   - Engineering checkpoints at 30/60/90 days and acceptance criteria to trigger reversion.
2) Service-credit cap: Reducing exposure to 2% or $10k is acceptable if Finance approves the $10k absolute cap for the expected ARR here. If CloudForge is larger than our threshold, we should use a percentage cap with a hard dollar maximum.
3) Commercial credit: 20% hosting credit months 1–3 is negotiable; legal prefers a fixed dollar credit cap instead of an open percentage.

I’ve looped Marissa (finance) to confirm the dollar caps and Rishi for final exec sign-off on the commercial concession. Please attach the proposed DocuSign amendment and legal redlines once available.

For transparency, we should record this as an SLA exception in the deal desk queue and link to the hubspot deal. I uploaded a redline (proposed-slo-redline.docx) to the shared drive and attached it here.

- Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-slo-redline.docx (docx)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Temporary SLO amendment & pricing relief during onboarding

Approved with conditions — I want to keep this narrow and measurable. Conditions: 

1) Approval window: 90 days only. Exception auto-expires; no rolling renewals without explicit re-approval.
2) SLO: 99.5% for the 90-day window.
3) Service-credit exposure: cap at the lesser of 2% monthly invoice or $10,000 (customer-facing cap).
4) Commercial concession: 20% credit months 1–3 but capped at $25,000 total across the three months.
5) Acceptance criteria: production go-live date must be confirmed and Redwood's SREs must be granted access to relevant import pipelines within 48 hours of go-live. If the customer does not provide cooperation, the commercial concession is void.
6) Legal to prepare a 1-page amendment (DocuSign) with the exact reversion language and telemetry checkpoints.

Vivek — proceed to get CloudForge's written agreement on the above and route the DocuSign to me for final signature. Naomi / Marissa: please confirm the accounting treatment and that the credit caps are acceptable.

Rishi
VP, Sales (Americas)
Redwood Inference
